coaching.title: Hill Repeats — 12 mi
coaching.message: Peak phase, 52 days out. Today's the specific session: 2 mi easy warm-up, then 12x 90-sec hard uphills, 2 mi cool-down. Drive the climbs into Zone 3-4 (155-175 bpm), power-hike the steepest pitches with hands on quads and let HR settle back toward 140 on each recovery down. This is exactly the alpine load Julian Alps' ~2500m of vert will demand — practice a strong, quiet upper body and short quick steps on the climbs. Note: your calendar had a stale 'Rest Day' entry for today, but the more recently updated session is these hill repeats, so we're running.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Top off with 30-40g carbs 30-60 min pre-run (banana + toast or a gel). It's under 2 hrs so you don't strictly need mid-session fuel, but take one gel (~25g carbs) around rep 6 to keep training the gut at the 60-80g/hr race target. Within 30 min of finishing: 25-30g protein plus carbs (chocolate milk or a shake + rice) to refill the glycogen you burned on the climbs.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Hard uphills tax the calves, quads and Achilles hardest. Post-run, 5-10 min easy walk to flush, then 10 min targeted mobility: calf raises to eccentric lowers, hip flexor and quad stretch, and foam roll quads and glutes. Elevate legs tonight and aim for 8+ hrs sleep — the adaptation from today's climbs happens overnight.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Every one of these 12 reps is a rehearsal for the long grinding climbs in the Julian Alps, where the race is won on the ascents. When the burn hits mid-rep, that's the exact feeling you'll meet at 30K in Slovenia — practice staying calm, holding form, and counting to the top. Peak phase is where the fitness gets built. Trust the work.
